title: Magnolia Telemetry — Onramp Field Notes
notes:
Meeting summary:
- 2026-01-18 discovery call with Magnolia (product telemetry team).
- Goal: ingest application telemetry (events + traces) to inform dynamic routing and cost-aware model selection in their customer-facing assistant. Must run in their VPC (air-gapped evaluation initially).

Attendees:
- Magnolia: Priya Desai (Lead SRE), Marco Li (Product Manager), Sofia Alvarez (Security)
- Redwood: Asha Kapoor (SE, owner), Daniel Ortiz (SRE lead), Clara Huang (PM liaison)

Key non-functional requirements noted:
- Data residency: telemetry (event-level) must not leave EU region for initial pilot.
- Network: customer will provide a private peering to our control-plane endpoint; data plane must run inside their VPC.
- Auth & keys: must integrate with customer KMS (HashiCorp vault + AWS KMS master key) and support HSM-wrapped model keys for encryption-at-rest.
- Latency SLO: 95th percentile token latency target 120ms for short prompts (<128 tokens) during business hours.
- Throughput: expect bursty traffic up to 250 QPS for reranking/embedding calls during product events.
- Retention & audit: event logs must be retained 90 days, admin audit trail for model rollouts required.

Technical constraints / gotchas (from call):
1) On premises telemetry agents: Magnolia runs Vector + OpenTelemetry collector with gRPC export to a local collector — need to provide a collector config snippet, not just endpoint.
2) Mutual TLS: their security team requires mTLS for all control-plane traffic and client cert rotation every 30 days.
3) Private deploy packaging: they want a minimal air-gapped bundle (OCI images + TLS assets) for initial install; ops will run the runtime on two dedicated GPU hosts behind an internal LB.
4) Quantization & model variants: Magnolia is sensitive to inference quality drift; they want automated A/B compare between float16 and int8 quantized variants with canary rollout. Need to expose evaluation hooks.
5) Telemetry volume: raw event payloads are large (many attributes). We should propose prefix/KV caching and a trimming policy, plus a small pre-ingest enrichment step to avoid sending full traces to model servers.
6) Schema mismatch: their event schema includes nested arrays and base64-encoded attachments; Redwood ingestion expects flattened JSON — provide transformation example or recommend using a preprocessing lambda.

Examples / suggestions to share (technical):
- Collector snippet (OTel) to send condensed events to Redwood ingress:
  exporters:
    otlp/mTLS:
      endpoint: "redwood-ingest.magnolia.local:4317"
      tls:
        cert_file: "/etc/collector/certs/client.crt"
        key_file: "/etc/collector/certs/client.key"
        ca_file: "/etc/collector/certs/ca.crt"
      headers:
        x-org-id: "magnolia-prod"

- Pre-ingest transform (pseudo): trim attributes >256 chars, drop attachments, compute event_hash, and include sampling_weight.

Operational notes:
- Recommend dedicated inference pool with autoscale disabled for pilot so we can control capacity and avoid noisy neighbors.
- Suggest enabling prefix/KV caching for repeated session context; customer sessions are long-lived for chat.
- For auditing model rollouts, expose webhook to Magnolia's CI to pull diffs and evaluation metrics.

Risk areas to flag to customer:
- If we run quantized int8 variants for throughput, small changes in prompts may surface hallucination differences — we need a prompt-based regression suite.
- mTLS cert rotation adds ops overhead; propose automation via cert-manager or a token-based short-lived cert flow.
- Network egress rules: some test infra attempted to reach S3 for model artifacts; ensure initial air-gapped bundle includes all model weights and runtime plugins.

Action items (owner / due):
- Asha: produce minimal OTel collector config + pre-ingest transform examples (due 2026-01-25).
- Daniel: prepare private-deploy packaging checklist (images, manifest, cert rotation docs) and test-run on local k8s (due 2026-02-02).
- Clara: draft high-level SLA and rollout checklist for Magnolia legal/security review (due 2026-01-28).
- Priya (Magnolia): provide sample event payloads (3-5 representative events) and network topology diagram (due 2026-01-22).
- Marco (Magnolia): confirm expected peak QPS window and retention policy (due 2026-01-20).

Follow-ups / next meetings:
- Tech deep-dive (21 days after sample payloads received) to map ingestion pipeline and verify transforms.
- Security review sync (mTLS and KMS/HSM integration) — invite Redwood security.

Notes to self / brainstorm items:
- Could offer a lightweight on-host preprocessor written in Go that runs as a sidecar to the OTel collector to perform flattening + sampling; easier for air-gapped installs.
- Consider exposing a local-only administrative UI for Magnolia to approve model rollouts in a manual-first mode.
- Evaluate using a deterministic embedding cache to reduce embedding QPS for repeated session context.

Immediate deliverables attached to linked_artifacts above. Keep doc status = draft until we confirm packaging and their security checklist.

-- Asha K.
